title: Right-angled and non-right-angled trigonometry

points.text: sin, cos and tan ratios in right-angled triangles
Sine rule, cosine rule and the ½ab sin C area formula

bigPicture: SOH CAH TOA solves right-angled triangles; the sine and cosine rules solve any triangle. Choose by what you know.

keyIdeas.answer: sin = opp/hyp, cos = adj/hyp, tan = opp/adj (not in the booklet).

keyIdeas.cue: When to use sine rule vs cosine rule?
keyIdeas.answer: Sine rule: a matched side-angle pair is known. Cosine rule: two sides and the included angle, or all three sides. Area = ½ab sin C uses the included angle.

keyIdeas.cue: How are triangle sides labelled, and what goes where in the cosine rule?
keyIdeas.answer: Side a is opposite angle A, b opposite B, c opposite C. In c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C, the side being squared on the left must be opposite the angle in the cosine. With two sides and an angle that is not between them, the cosine rule gives a quadratic for the third side: discard a negative root; two positive roots mean two possible triangles.

keyIdeas.cue: On Paper 1, how do you use the area or cosine rule when you only know cos C (or sin C) as a fraction?
keyIdeas.answer: Use sin²C + cos²C = 1. For example cos C = 3/5 gives sin C = 4/5 (positive because 0° < C < 180°), which goes straight into ½ab sin C. No angle in degrees is needed.

keyTerms.def: angle between the two given sides

misconceptions.wrong: Sine rule with no matched pair
misconceptions.right: You need one side and its opposite angle.

misconceptions.wrong: An angle found from the area formula has one value.
misconceptions.right: ½ab sin C = area gives sin C = k, so C could be acute or obtuse (C or 180° − C). Check which fit the information.

misconceptions.wrong: Knowing all three angles fixes the triangle.
misconceptions.right: Three angles fix only the shape; you need at least one length. Also, any two sides must add up to more than the third.

practice.prompt: In triangle PQR, PQ = 6, PR = 10 and angle QPR = 60°. Find QR exactly and the exact area.
commonErrors: Using a non-included angle in the area

practice.prompt: In triangle ABC, AB = 8 cm, angle A = 52°, angle B = 71°. Find BC and the area.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.
